research_goal: Design and implement repository separation for deployable desktop apps, project-local history, cross-project control records, and standalone platform-desktop-app builds.
coding_context: Existing Tauri/Next.js desktop app with Node snapshot collector, TypeScript snapshot model, React project management panel, CSS, and node:test contract tests.
source_value_provenance: Git official docs establish submodule control-plane behavior and the need to explicitly manage separate repository checkouts.
GitHub Actions checkout documentation shows submodule checkout is explicit CI behavior, not a default release assumption.
GitHub releases documentation supports release artifacts belonging to the deployable repository.
Local source shows Workspace Monitor currently has registry and snapshot patterns that can absorb repository topology without new dependencies.
plan_evidence: All active root projects are already submodules, so the safer change is release-root and history-boundary separation rather than destructive folder splitting.
Existing customer snapshot sanitization provides the right boundary for excluding raw cross-project history.
The collector root fallback is the deployment risk because standalone app clones should not require the workspace control repository.
stack_version_constraints: Use existing workspace-monitor and platform-desktop-app dependencies.
No new package install is needed.
Rust/Tauri runtime remains unchanged in this slice.
issue_discussion_sources: explicit none-found discussion record: no external issue discussion is needed because this slice is grounded in official Git/GitHub docs and local deployment source.
issue_discussion_notes: User-reported deployment difficulty is the primary local problem signal.
Community signals are not used as factual proof.
community_signal_notes: No stars, votes, likes, or forum comments are used for claims.
CI/submodule risk is treated as a deployment design risk from official docs.
language_decision_notes: The change is snapshot data, UI, and tests, all currently owned by TypeScript/React/Node.
Rust/Tauri changes would add runtime risk without solving repository topology visibility.
Shell-only changes would not give users a visible app contract.
architecture_options: Keep root workspace as deployment source and require submodule checkout.
Release each desktop app from its own repository and keep root as control plane.
Create a new history ledger immediately and move all _history records now.
architecture_decision_notes: Selected app-repo release root plus root control plane because it reduces release blast radius without destructive migration.
Rejected root deployment because signing, updater, and customer snapshot review should not depend on every project submodule.
Rejected immediate full _history move because it requires compatibility indexing and could break current validators.
architecture_tradeoff_notes: The selected design keeps current submodule visibility while making deployment independent.
History is split by policy first; physical ledger migration remains explicit and auditable.
Customer builds become easier, but developer snapshots can still opt into MONITOR_REPO_ROOT.
code_reference_notes: Existing collector modules read self-documenting registries and sanitize customer snapshots.
Existing project management UI uses feature panels with data attributes for tests.
Existing tests validate collector shape and UI source contracts.
folder_structure_options: Put repository topology in root _ops only.
Put repository topology in platform-desktop-app/configs and expose via app snapshot.
Put repository topology inside release-runbook only.
folder_structure_decision_notes: Selected platform-desktop-app/configs because release topology governs the desktop app's build and UI.
Root _ops alone would not be available in standalone app releases.
Runbook-only text would not be machine-checkable or visible in the app.
folder_semantics_notes: platform-desktop-app/docs owns release and topology documentation.
_history records cross-project work evidence until a ledger migration exists.
maintainability_notes: The registry is self-documenting and validated.
Standalone root support is tested with a temp app repo fixture.
Customer sanitization is tested separately from developer topology output.
findings: The current submodule separation is useful for portfolio tracking but should not be the app release root.
Deployment should default to app-local configs/docs/specs and use MONITOR_REPO_ROOT only for developer portfolio snapshots.
History should be project-local first, with future ledger migration for cross-project records.
options: App release repo plus control-plane root
recommendation: Implement app release repo plus control-plane root, add repository topology registry/UI, and keep physical history ledger migration as an explicit future migration.

post_research_answers.what_was_verified: Submodule docs, CI checkout behavior, release ownership, current submodule state, current collector root behavior, and UI/test extension points.
post_research_answers.best_option: App release repo plus control-plane root.
post_research_answers.why_this_option: It addresses deployment difficulty now without destructive history migration.
post_research_answers.alternatives_rejected: Root release repo keeps deployment too coupled; immediate full ledger split risks breaking history validators.
post_research_answers.implementation_impact: Add registry, collector module, snapshot type, UI panel, CSS, tests, docs, and close-out records.
post_research_answers.risks_and_unknowns: Actual new history ledger repository is still pending a migration plan.
post_research_answers.validation_plan: Config contract, target tests, TypeScript, check, build, customer bundle audit, browser smoke, omission/resource/evaluation guards.
post_research_answers.reusable_knowledge: The topology registry becomes the durable contract for future release and history moves.
post_research_answers.next_action: Finish validation, commit app repo, update control repo pointer, and push both.

risks_or_unknowns: Future workspace-history-ledger repository is not created in this slice.
Existing legacy _history remains in the root control plane until a migration plan is validated.
Public signing/notarization remains a separate release readiness gate.
